text: Time for actual string functions. We'll start with three of the simplest and most common: LEN for length, UPPER and LOWER for changing case.
LEN of first name, as name length. Straightforward — it counts the characters in a string. Useful for spotting unusually short or long values, or just validating your data.

But here's a genuine gotcha: LEN of the string Hello with three trailing spaces returns 5, not 8. LEN ignores trailing spaces when counting — though leading spaces still count normally. This rarely matters with VARCHAR data, which doesn't naturally pick up trailing spaces. But remember CHAR from Lesson 41 — it pads values with trailing spaces to hit its declared length, and LEN simply won't count that padding. A real trap if you're not expecting it.

UPPER converts every letter to uppercase; LOWER converts every letter to lowercase. And just like every function you've used so far, neither one touches the actual stored data — they only affect what shows up in your query's output.

One practical use: wrapping both sides of a comparison in UPPER guarantees a case-insensitive match, regardless of what the server's default settings happen to be. LEN counts characters, ignoring trailing spaces; UPPER and LOWER reshape case in your output only. Next lesson: SUBSTRING and CHARINDEX, for pulling specific pieces out of a string. See you there.
